source_refs.title: Eureka Math / EngageNY, Grade 1, Module 1, Lesson 1

subject: math

objective.text: Find numbers hiding inside a number up to 10. Show them with 5-groups and number bonds.

explanations.title: Number detectives
explanations.text: Let's be number detectives! A number can have smaller numbers hiding inside it. Look at 5 beads. I can see 2 hiding inside the 5.

explanations.title: Total and parts (number bond)
explanations.text: A number bond shows a big number and the parts hiding inside it. The big number is the total, or the whole. The smaller numbers are the parts. 2 and 3 are the parts of 5.

explanations.title: Five and some more (5-group way)
explanations.text: Look at 7 beads. There is a row of 5 and 2 more. Draw 5 dots for one part and 2 dots for the other part. Now count on from 5: five, 6, 7. The total is 7.

explanations.title: Fingers the Math Way
explanations.text: You can show numbers with your fingers. To show 6, hold up all 5 fingers on one hand and 1 finger on the other hand. Can you see the 5 inside the 6?

examples.title: Parts of 5: 2 and 3
examples.text: 5 beads are in the top row. Cover 2 beads. The other part is 3. Number bond: total 5, parts 2 and 3.

examples.title: Parts of 7: 5 and 2
examples.text: 7 beads: 5 in the top row and 2 in the bottom row. Number bond: total 7, parts 5 and 2. Count on from 5: five, 6, 7.

questions.text: I will show some fingers very fast. Look carefully! How many fingers did you see?
Here are 5 fingers on one hand. Now I show 2 more fingers on the other hand. Count on from 5. How many fingers in all?
There are 5 beads in the top row. Cover 2 of them. What is the other part of 5?
2 and 3 are parts of 5. Can you find two different parts that make 5?
Now there are 7 beads: 5 in the top row and 2 in the bottom row. Cover the 5. What is the other part of 7?
You have 5 dots as one part and 2 dots as the other part. Count on from 5 to find the total. What is the total?
Look at 7 beads. What numbers can you see hiding inside the 7? Tell me how you see them.
Eight fingernails have nail polish. One hand has 5 fingernails. Make 5 one part of the number bond. What is the other part of 8?
Six fingernails have nail polish. One hand has 5 fingernails. Make 5 one part of the number bond. What is the other part of 6?
Dora found 5 leaves that blew in through the window. Then she found 2 more leaves. How many leaves did Dora find in all? Show your thinking.
Look at 8 soccer balls and 9 pencils. What is the same about them?

misconceptions.label: Touch and count instead of seeing the 5-group
misconceptions.description: Child counts every object from 1 instead of seeing the 5 (or a group of 2 or 3) and counting on. The right total can still come out, but the child is not yet seeing embedded numbers.
detection_signals: Answer is a count from 1 (for example '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7') when counting on from 5 was asked.
Child cannot name the 5 or any other part inside the number.
misconceptions.response_text: Nice counting! Here is a faster way. You can see the 5 right away. Start at 5, then count on: five, 6, 7.

assets_required.why_this_method: Finger counts must be exact and follow the Math Way order. Diffusion often draws extra or missing fingers.
assets_required.description: Two hands shown from the child's view. Fingers appear for a short time, then hide.
must_show_exactly: Exactly N fingers raised for N = 0-10
Fingers fill left to right from the child's view
6 = five fingers on one hand plus the thumb of the other hand (source p26)
states_or_frames: Flash sequence: hidden -> show N for display_seconds (default 2) -> hidden
Count-on sequence: show 5-hand, then add fingers one at a time
assets_required.interaction: Timed display. No child interaction while shown. Answer comes after hide.
assets_required.review_notes: Source says hand order depends on whether the teacher faces the class or a document camera (p22). Check the order against the child's screen view.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat cartoon child's hands held up facing the viewer, N fingers raised (N = 0 to 10), plain light background, no extra fingers. [Build N=0-10 as 11 poses by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: Needs exact slots, draggable beads and a cover action. This is behaviour, not a picture.
assets_required.description: A board of 10 slots in 2 rows of 5. Beads fill the top row left to right first.
must_show_exactly: Beads placed 0-10, top row filled first, left to right
Bead count always matches the question stimulus
states_or_frames: cover state: chosen beads hidden by a cover
assets_required.interaction: Drag beads in. Tap beads to cover or uncover them. Tutor can set the bead count from the question stimulus.
assets_required.alt_text: A box of 10 slots in two rows of 5 with beads in some slots.
assets_required.generation_caption: Simple flat board with 10 round slots in 2 rows of 5, colourful beads in some slots, plain background, child-friendly.

assets_required.why_this_method: A fixed diagram with input boxes. Needs exact labels and behaviour.
assets_required.description: Number bond: one total circle at the top joined by lines to two part circles below (labelled total, part, part in the source).
must_show_exactly: Each box accepts a numeral OR 5-group dots (source p25)
assets_required.interaction: Child (or tutor) fills boxes. Boxes can be shown covered or hidden for 'find the missing part'.
assets_required.alt_text: A number bond with a total on top and two parts below.
assets_required.generation_caption: Clean number bond diagram: one big circle on top joined by two lines to two smaller circles below, empty boxes, bright simple colours.

assets_required.why_this_method: Dot counts and row layout must be exact. Diffusion cannot do this.
assets_required.description: Dots drawn the 5-group way: a row of 5, then the rest in a second row.
must_show_exactly: First 5 in one row, remaining dots in the next row
Parts can be drawn in different colours
states_or_frames: dot-by-dot count-on highlight starting at the 5th dot
assets_required.interaction: Highlight dots one by one for counting on. Optional draw mode for the child.
assets_required.alt_text: N dots arranged in a row of five and a row of the rest.
assets_required.generation_caption: N bright round dots in a row of five with the rest in a second row, on a white background, flat style.

assets_required.why_this_method: Needs exactly 5 fingernails per hand and a colourable nail per finger. Diffusion often draws wrong finger counts. Diffusion may be used only for a decorative background.
assets_required.description: Two cartoon hands with 10 fingernails. Nails are coloured left to right to show the number in the question.
must_show_exactly: Total coloured nails = 8 for q_ps_5 and 6 for q_ps_6
assets_required.interaction: Display only. Child answers by voice or typing.
assets_required.alt_text: Two hands with some fingernails painted.
assets_required.generation_caption: Two friendly cartoon hands, 5 fingers each, visible fingernails, 8 nails painted pink (second version: 6 nails painted), flat vector style.

assets_required.why_this_method: Diffusion may draw ONE soccer ball icon and ONE pencil icon in a child-friendly style. Code must tile them so the counts are exact.
assets_required.description: A set of 8 soccer balls and a set of 9 pencils, each arranged so a group of 5 is easy to see.
must_show_exactly: Each set laid out as 5 + the rest (5-group way)
assets_required.alt_text: Eight soccer balls and nine pencils, each set in a row of five and the rest.

review_flags.item: Problem Set items 1-4 and 7-12, Exit Ticket 1-2, Homework 1-16
review_flags.issue: These are picture-only items. The extracted text has no numbers or answer keys. Not added as questions. Needs human or vision extraction from the PDF images.
Card is a DRAFT made by an AI. Not reviewed. Needs the content review in the pipeline doc before publishing.
k_counting_to_10 and k_number_bonds are Kindergarten cards that do not exist yet. The source only points to K.CC standards, it does not teach these.

The source states only one misconception (touch and count). Not added, because they are not in the source: giving the total instead of the missing part (for example 7 for q_pr_3), and mixing up total and part. Add them only after review.
All 4 variants come from one teaching approach in the source. There is no truly different alternative (for example a number line). The Planner has little real choice for now.
The source has few hints. The 6 hints are adapted from teacher notes and instructions. Level 3 and wording need review.
The source never says whether 0 and 5 count as parts of 5. Left out of valid_pairs. Decide with the team.
Single-number answers have no real partial outcome. The script must map partial to the same path as incorrect, or the shared schema must allow null.
The source gives no answer and keeps this open on purpose. The key (7) is derived from 5 + 2. A child who draws instead of speaking or typing needs a widget.
The source is a teacher script for a 60-minute class with objects. All child-facing text was rewritten for a screen. Needs age-appropriate wording review.
All 7 assets are marked not_available. Each has a visual spec (method, exact counts, frames). Items that use them cannot be launched until the asset exists.
Only K.CC.2, K.CC.4 and K.CC.5 appear in this lesson file. The Grade 1 standard is in the Module Overview and was not added.
Source is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Cards made from it must keep attribution to Great Minds, stay non-commercial, and share under the same license. Check this before any paid deployment.
Diffusion cannot be trusted for counts. Use code-rendered visuals for anything with exact numbers, and have a person check each visual against the answer key.
Finger order depends on the viewer's side (source p22 and p26). Check the orientation for the child's screen.
Use an original character. Do not draw any known cartoon character.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
